# PR #970: Add sort by for chats

- PR: https://github.com/EratoLab/erato/pull/970
- Status: pending (diff reviewed)
- Category: Features and enhancements
- Theme: None

## Summary

**The PR's auto-generated description significantly undersells this
change.** It describes only a backend chat-type filter (`RecentChatTypeFilter`,
chat vs. assistant) and some frontend query-cache/type-safety fixes, but
the diff (3379 insertions across 28 files) actually ships a full sidebar
filter-and-group-by menu with persisted user preferences — confirmed by
reading the new `chatHistoryFilterStore.ts` and `chatHistoryGrouping.ts`
in full:

- New `useChatHistoryFilterStore` (Zustand, persisted per browser via
  `persist` middleware, so the sidebar's filter/sort state survives a
  reload): a **type filter** (`all`/`chat`/`assistant`), a **status
  filter** (`active`/`all`, presumably active-vs-archived), and a
  **group-by** setting (`date`/`type`/`unread`/`none`) — confirmed as
  distinct, independently togglable axes, with helper functions
  distinguishing "a filter that can exclude rows is active"
  (`hasActiveFilters`, excludes grouping, which only rearranges rows) from
  "everything is at its out-of-the-box default" (`isDefaultFilters`).
- New `chatHistoryGrouping.ts` (171 lines, read in part): client-side
  bucketing of the sidebar's chat sessions for the "Group by date" option
  — recent calendar days each get their own dated bucket (localized via
  `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, DST-safe day-age rounding), older chats fall into
  a catch-all bucket. A shared `resolveChatAttentionStatus` classifier
  determines a row's status indicator, with an unresolved tool-approval
  confirmation (from #918) explicitly outranking the chat's own generation
  status (from #868) — used both for the status dot and for the "Unread"
  group-by bucket.
- Backend: `RecentChatTypeFilter` enum (`chat`/`assistant`) is threaded
  through `RecentChatsFilter`, the SQL query, and the public
  `GET /me/chats` API as a new query parameter, alongside the existing
  `pinned` (#943) and `q` search filters — not independently re-verified
  beyond the type/enum wiring, but consistent with the established filter-
  parameter pattern from #943's `pinned` addition.
- A new `ChatHistoryFilterMenu.tsx` (574 lines, the single largest new
  file — not read in detail) presumably surfaces these filter/group-by
  options as an actual UI control in the sidebar, given its size and the
  associated 278-line test file.
- Also confirmed present (not independently verified in detail): a shared
  `mapRecentChatToSession` utility consolidating previously-duplicated
  chat-session mapping logic, and fixes to generated TypeScript codegen
  types for `is_pinned`/`title_by_summary`/`title_by_user_provided` fields
  that were apparently missing or mistyped.

## Compatibility and configuration

None new server-side beyond the additive `RecentChatTypeFilter` query
parameter (backward compatible — omitting it presumably defaults to no
filtering). Frontend: the sidebar's filter/group-by preferences are now
persisted to browser storage per the user, defaulting to
`{typeFilter: "all", statusFilter: "active", groupBy: "date"}` — matching
the sidebar's existing default appearance for a first-time or
never-customized user.

Verified via this PR's squash-merge commit against its parent (both
present locally). Read in full: the complete `chatHistoryFilterStore.ts`
and the header/grouping-by-date portion of `chatHistoryGrouping.ts` —
this is how the description gap was found: the auto-generated PR body
never mentions a filter/group-by UI at all, prompting direct
investigation of the large new files the diff stat revealed. Given the
substantial remaining scope, the following were not read in detail: the
574-line `ChatHistoryFilterMenu.tsx` (the actual UI control), the

rendered list), the 199-line `useChatHistory.ts` diff, the backend
`models/chat.rs`/`server/api/v1beta/mod.rs` diffs implementing the new

6+ test files.

## Release note disposition

Proposed category: Features and enhancements. Worth a clear, specific
mention (the terse PR title undersells it too): the chat history sidebar
now has a filter/sort menu — filter by chat type (regular chat vs.
assistant conversation) or by active/archived status, and group the list
by date, type, or unread status — with the chosen preferences remembered
across sessions.
